messages:
lee_support: Hey team — customer ACME (org_id: org_9823) opened a support ticket: managers in their org see empty dashboards for ‘team-activity’ and ‘latency-by-route’ for the last 90 days. Individual contributors see data. Ticket #2345. Repro steps attached.

dana_analytics: Can you paste org_id + one manager user_id and a screenshot? which specific charts are blank?

lee_support: org_9823, manager user_id u_9932. Screenshot: https://intranet/screens/2345.png (customer redacted). Members view OK, managers’ time series show flat "no data". Important: when customer hits the /events API with the manager's token they get events back for older dates. Example curl below.

lee_support: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token-for-u_9932>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/org_9823/events?start=2024-08-01&end=2024-11-01" -i
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
[ {"event_id":"e1","ts":"2024-09-15T12:00:00Z","route":"/generate"}, ... ]```

arjun_product: Interesting — API returns events but console charts are empty for the same role. Suspect a retention/permission layer on the analytics timeseries index that filters by role TTL. Any chance a migration or config change recently targeted role scopes?

sam_sre: Looking at logs and index writes for org_9823: I see a bad migration job (deploy 4572) that set retention_ttl=0 for roles matching /manager/ due to a malformed predicate. Log snippet: 

"INFO 2024-11-25 09:12:03 migration-runner - applying retention override: role=manager, retention_days=0, scope=role"

That would cause the timeseries index to drop or hide data for role-scoped queries. The underlying raw events are still in object storage (S3), but the timeseries materialized view obeys TTL.

deploy-bot: Deployment 4572: retention-migration v2 -> success (2024-11-25T09:12:05Z) :rocket:

sam_sre: Proposed remediation: 1) revert the migration predicate locally, 2) set retention_ttl to org_default (90) for affected role entries, 3) trigger a backfill to rebuild aggregates for the 90-day window. SQL we ran in staging: 

```-- set role retention back to default for affected rows
UPDATE analytics.role_retention
SET retention_days = 90
WHERE org_id = 'org_9823' AND role_name ILIKE '%manager%';

-- enqueue backfill job
INSERT INTO analytics.backfill_jobs (org_id, started_by, range_start, range_end)
VALUES ('org_9823','sam_sre','2024-08-01','2024-11-01');```

dana_analytics: Backfill note: when you run the rebuild, ensure we re-run the per-route rollups and not just per-user aggregates — dashboards query aggregated tables. Command we use: `./tools/run_backfill --org org_9823 --start 2024-08-01 --end 2024-11-01 --type rollup`

lee_support: Two questions from customer: (1) Will any historical raw events be permanently lost? (2) ETA for fix/backfill so we can reply?

arjun_product: (1) No raw events lost — TTL only affected timeseries/materialized view retention, raw S3 is intact. (2) Hotfix applied to staging, plan to push to prod in 2h with maintenance window; backfill expected ~30–45 minutes after hotfix for that org. We should give customer a 3hr ETA to be safe.

sam_sre: Executed hotfix at 2024-11-25T11:02:00Z — updated role_retention rows and started backfill job id bf_778. Monitoring current.

sam_sre: Update: backfill job completed successfully at 2024-11-25T11:36:12Z, aggregates rebuilt. I can see time series for manager role returning values now.

lee_support: Confirmed with customer — dashboards populated again. Closing ticket #2345. Customer asked for post-mortem. Filing one and including rollback details + how migration predicate was malformed. :white_check_mark:
